sections.h2: How a Taylor homeowner can sell without a long wait
sections.html:
A Taylor owner may hire an agent, locate a buyer privately, or accept cash from someone willing to take the house as it stands. The house itself often decides, since Downriver neighborhoods like Taylor hold many older, modestly priced homes where repair bills can exceed what owners expected.

The median home value is $152,600. An owner whose roof or furnace has failed may have no savings left to fix it first, and a direct purchase of the house as is becomes worth a look.

  • Agent listing: strongest price potential when the house shows well and a financed buyer can be waited out.
  • Do it yourself: saves the commission, yet you still need a purchase agreement, title work and a recorded deed.
  • Cash sale: no repairs or open houses, with the closing date negotiated in the contract.

One Taylor rule affects every route: the city wants a certificate of occupancy whenever ownership changes, as explained below.

Taylor spans about 23.6 square miles of Wayne County and has 61,279 people as of 2025. Dearborn Heights is its northern neighbor, and Allen Park and Southgate touch its eastern line. I-94 passes through the north end, I-75 clips the southeast, and Telegraph Road (US 24) serves as the main spine. Shopping is concentrated along Eureka Road around Southland Shopping Center.

Buyer budgets drive this market. Two of every three homes have owner occupants, and the population is down 3.3% since 2020, so buyers have choices and price carefully.

sections.h2: Certificate of occupancy when a house is sold
sections.html:
Yes, Taylor requires one. Under Zoning Ordinance Section 25.06, ownership changes call for a certificate of occupancy before anyone moves in. One certificate covers a single owner's time holding the house and does not pass to the next buyer.

This matters when you accept a fast offer. If the buyer cannot move in until the city issues the certificate, a repair item raised in the inspection can hold up occupancy. Ask the Building Department at 734-287-6550 what an inspector will check, and whether anything on the house could fail. The department is at 23555 Goddard Road, and its building inspectors keep short office hours each weekday morning and late afternoon.

Exterior work such as fences, siding, windows, roofing and concrete needs a permit, as does interior work that changes structure. Painting, tile and carpet do not. No work can start until a permit has been issued, so pull permits for any repair you make before closing.

sections.h2: Your first week as a Taylor seller
sections.html:
Begin with a few calls and one printout. A short list keeps a quick sale moving.

  • Print the current tax bill from the city's online tax lookup, which shows the balance and any penalty.
  • Call the Building Department at 734-287-6550 about the certificate of occupancy and any open permits.
  • Request a lender payoff letter when a mortgage remains.
  • Collect the lease and rental certificate if tenants live in the house.
  • Choose whether a title company or an attorney will prepare the deed for the Wayne County Register of Deeds.

Each task is small, and together they head off most surprises in a buyer's title search.

sections.h2: Selling a rented house in Taylor
sections.html:
Rental houses carry their own paperwork. City code Article V, Sections 8-100 through 8-111, calls for registration and a rental certificate of compliance, which stays valid three years and must be renewed before it lapses. Fines run $150 for a first violation, $250 for a second and $500 afterward, and each day can count separately.

Give a buyer both the lease and the current certificate. A new owner inherits the same duties, so a missing certificate becomes that owner's first expense.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips, and what it doesn't
sections.html:
A cash buyer doesn't need a lender's appraisal, so the wait for loan approval drops out of the schedule, and you can negotiate the closing date in the contract. The city rules still apply. The certificate of occupancy, the tax proration and the deed recording all happen no matter how the buyer pays. Ask the buyer early who handles the Building Department call, who pays the recording fee and whether any open permit on the house needs to be closed first.

At closing, expect the title company to pay off your mortgage from the proceeds, settle any tax balance, and send the deed to the Register of Deeds for recording.

The Taylor School District has a single comprehensive high school, Taylor High on Beech Daly Road. Charter options include Taylor Preparatory High School, Taylor Exemplar Academy and Trillium Academy. Municipal buildings cluster along Goddard Road near Telegraph, and Northline Road leads to the Wayne County Community College District's Downriver campus. Name the school district in your listing, since families ask about it first.

Wayne County prints its levies on the register's page: county $0.55 and state $3.75, each per $500 of the price. The grantor pays them when the deed is recorded, and MCL 207.523 names the seller as liable. A deed qualifying for an exemption skips the tax, provided it cites the lettered subsection of MCL 207.526 or MCL 207.505.

Recording itself costs $30.00 per document since January 1, 2026: a $26.00 fee and a $4.00 state survey and remonumentation charge. Warranty deeds need a Wayne County Treasurer tax certification beforehand. The recording desk answers at (313) 224-5851, and the office suggests having an attorney prepare the deed.

sections.h2: Tax bills around a Taylor closing
sections.html:
The summer bill is due September 30, and the winter bill falls due in mid-February. A real property balance still open on March 1 goes to the Wayne County Treasurer, and a second unpaid year exposes the house to tax foreclosure. Taylor cuts the summer bill along a July 1 to June 30 year and the winter bill along December 1 to November 30, so closing proration follows those periods.

Homeowners 62 or older whose income stayed below $40,000 can defer the summer bill by applying before September 30. Delinquent water charges and unpaid ordinance citations may be added to a bill as special assessments. Taxable value uncaps in the calendar year after a transfer, so a buyer should plan for a larger bill. The assessor's number is 734-374-1315.

If taxes are owed when you sell, the title agent deducts the balance from your proceeds at closing, so ask for a payoff figure before you set the date.

faqs.q: Is an inspection part of selling in Taylor?
faqs.a: The city issues a certificate of occupancy to the new owner after any ownership change, and the Building Department at 734-287-6550 can explain what its inspector looks at.

faqs.q: What is the Wayne County cost to record a deed?
faqs.a: A flat $30.00 per document, effective January 1, 2026. Transfer tax comes on top unless the deed is exempt.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller owe Taylor transfer tax?
faqs.a: The statute puts it on the seller. A purchase agreement can assign it to the buyer by agreement.

faqs.q: What if taxes are late when I sell my Taylor house?
faqs.a: After March 1 the balance sits with the county treasurer, and the title agent deducts what is owed from your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Are rented houses treated differently in Taylor?
faqs.a: Yes. They need registration and a three-year certificate of compliance, with fines starting at $150 for a violation.
